video_title: Scaling Linear's GTM to $100M+ ARR — Cristina Cordova, COO
gist: Linear COO Cristina Cordova explains how Linear grew at least 10x in ~3.5 years with a lean (~170-person), no-SDR, in-house-support model, sequencing from startups to growth-stage to enterprise (launched 2025), and how it pivoted to agent orchestration after CEO Kari's 'task tracking is dead' post, with over 50% of issues now created by agents. The transcript (an auto-translated caption track) never states the $100M+ ARR figure from the title.

themes.theme: Task tracking is dead: Linear's agent pivot

insights.claim: Linear's CEO Kari published a post declaring 'task tracking is dead'; Cordova frames it as Linear deliberately escaping the innovator's dilemma that pre-AI tools face, rather than defending a workflow (manual ticket tracking) that likely won't exist in a few years.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Incumbent SaaS that cannibalize their own core category early may out-position larger peers locked into legacy revenue.
insights.quote: we probably shouldn't live in a world where people manually track work

insights.claim: Cordova argues Linear benefits from being small enough to reinvent itself, contrasting it with Google, for which putting an AI block above every search result and killing ad views would be very hard.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Scale is a liability in platform shifts; mid-size SaaS can pivot faster than mega-cap incumbents.
insights.quote: we are not big enough to destroy ourselves

insights.claim: Most Linear customers, when told about the 'task tracking is dead' post, agreed with it rather than being alarmed.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Customer buy-in suggests the repositioning reduces churn risk rather than creating it.
insights.quote: most of them agreed: yes, task tracking is dead

insights.claim: Linear is directing the vast majority of its resources toward a new category of agent orchestration / product-development system, while still remaining in the legacy issue-tracking category.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Signals Linear's R&D spend and roadmap are now AI-agent-first; watch for category-creation positioning versus Jira-style trackers.

insights.claim: Over 50% of issues in Linear are now created by agents, within roughly a year and a half of Linear launching its MCP server in 2025, which Cordova believes was the first in its niche.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Hard evidence agents are already the majority producer of work items in dev tooling; seat-based tracker models are exposed.
insights.quote: over 50% of tasks are in Linear created by agents

insights.claim: Cordova says in-app issue creation by humans is also rising alongside MCP usage, which she reads as proof Linear's UX serves both humans and agents; chat interfaces are single-player and poor for visualizing team work.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Counters the 'UI is dead, everything goes through chat' narrative for collaborative SaaS.
insights.quote: the chat interface often not the best way display all the work it does team

insights.claim: Cordova believes SaaS companies that merely become a database behind an MCP server and let external agents operate on the data will not have a good business model; agent workflows must be built into the tool itself so users still have reasons to come into the app.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Framework for judging SaaS durability in the agent era: own the agent workflow, not just the data.
insights.quote: But I don't think it will be good in the end. business model

insights.claim: Linear's features include 'loops', which auto-assigns an agent to an issue and has it start work such as writing code, and 'intelligent sorting'/triage that auto-labels, assigns and routes incoming bug reports and feature requests without the user building an agent.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Productized agents (not DIY) is Linear's wedge for less AI-forward customers.
insights.quote: not everything has to be agent. This may just be part of product

insights.claim: Linear is used by the vast majority of leading AI labs, and those AI-native customers pushed Linear toward agentic workflows, saying otherwise it would be the wrong product.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: AI-lab adoption is a leading indicator and a learning channel for broader enterprise demand.
insights.quote: the vast majority of top AI companies already using Linear

insights.claim: Pre-AI but cutting-edge companies such as Ramp and Coinbase built internal agents and asked Linear for APIs to create agents inside Linear while owning their data; Cordova says no competitor had such an API set at the time.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Agent platform APIs became a differentiator versus competitors in the enterprise segment.

insights.claim: In 2025 Linear built, without having planned any of it, an MCP server, an agent platform with new APIs, and partnerships with Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot so their agents work inside Linear, at the cost of deferring planned enterprise features like sub-teams and multi-level roadmaps.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Shows willingness to sacrifice roadmap for platform-shift positioning; integration partnerships with coding agents are now table stakes.

insights.claim: Cordova says because Linear shipped agent tooling while competitors procrastinated, many large companies added Linear to their consideration lists that otherwise would not have — the agent work pulled in enterprise demand indirectly.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Being first on agent-native features can substitute for classic enterprise feature checklists in winning large accounts.
insights.quote: our competitors have been doing it for a long time procrastinating

themes.theme: Enterprise GTM sequencing and sales design

insights.claim: When Cordova joined Linear (about 35–40 employees, ~2023), the company had no public-company customers and probably no customer above ~500 seats; it was mid-market at most, known as a startup product, and grew via product-led self-serve signups (e.g., Vercel, Ramp).
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Baseline for Linear's upmarket trajectory; PLG got it to mid-market without sales.

insights.claim: Linear has grown at least 10x since Cordova joined about three and a half years ago.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Implies strong multi-year compounding under a lean, sales-light model.
insights.quote: we grew up at least 10 times, in my opinion, since I joined

insights.claim: Three weeks after joining, Cordova publicly crossed out Linear's company goal of entering enterprise because there was literally one salesperson, refocusing instead on winning growth-stage companies that had to displace an incumbent tool; Linear only formally launched an enterprise segment in 2025.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Sequencing upmarket by proving displacement wins first is a template for PLG companies.
insights.quote: with one You won't enter the corporate market as a person

insights.claim: Cordova draws a parallel to Stripe, which for a long time mostly won brand-new businesses implementing payments for the first time before it could win companies switching from competitors; rip-and-replace sales take time.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Displacement sales lag greenfield wins; investors should expect enterprise ramp to trail PLG traction.

insights.claim: Cordova argues a product cannot be 20–30% better and expect people to switch because of switching costs; it must be significantly better, and Linear's founders, ex-Coinbase, Airbnb and Uber, knew firsthand that incumbent tools were disliked.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Displacement plays require step-change UX; founder-as-frustrated-user is a moat signal.
insights.quote: I don't think you can be 20 times better. %or 30%and force people to switch

insights.claim: Linear has no SDRs; Cordova believes SDR qualifying calls waste the technical buyer's time and that account executives should do their own outbound, supported by automation and tooling.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Leaner sales cost structure; challenges standard SaaS sales-org templates.
insights.quote: We have never had SDR

insights.claim: Linear hired account executives who already had experience selling technical products to demanding engineers and designers who want to skip slides and go to the demo, and requires sales reps to pass training certifications before selling.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Developer-tool sales talent is specialized; hiring profile drives win rate.

insights.claim: Linear's solution engineers sit in sales, partner with enterprise AEs on deep workflow, API and migration questions (e.g., migrating 30,000 people), and sometimes build end-to-end demos overnight, such as a ServiceNow integration; Linear does not use forward-deployed engineers inside customer systems, believing the product should be simple enough for anyone to integrate.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Contrasts with the trendy forward-deployed-engineer model; implies lower implementation cost per deal.

insights.claim: Cordova contrasts Linear's opinionated, narrower tool with competitors that are near-infinitely configurable and need dedicated in-house administrators; Linear's opinionated defaults make data easier to read across teams.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Opinionated product reduces TCO and admin headcount, a selling point versus configurable incumbents.

insights.claim: Enterprise sales cycles vary widely: one 1,000-person company switched in about a month after a top-down CEO decision, while another took two to two-and-a-half years, with champions repeatedly failing to convince the CTO; Linear's sellers coach internal champions to sell to IT and procurement.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Champion enablement is a core lever; deal timing remains lumpy and political.

insights.claim: In summer 2025, typically a slow season for Linear's business, demand did not slow down, which Cordova attributes to the AI-driven pace of launches; she says traditional launch-timing rules are obsolete until AI consolidation arrives.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Seasonality in dev-tool buying weakened in the AI cycle.

insights.claim: Cordova says decision speed at legacy enterprises hasn't really increased, but AI budgets have been unlocked — a supplementary, very large budget that appeared out of nowhere — and getting a tool classified into the AI budget makes purchase decisions much easier.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Positioning SaaS as 'AI spend' accesses new incremental budget; a key driver of current dev-tool revenue.
insights.quote: we magically found a budget that didn't exist before

insights.claim: Cordova predicts the current enterprise AI experimentation wave, driven by fear that 'our company will die' without trying tools, will stop in a year or two once companies learn what works; buyers now prefer one-year or pilot contracts over three-year deals.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Risk of churn/consolidation for AI tools riding experimental budgets; contract durations are shortening.
insights.quote: at some point, maybe in a year or so two, it will stop

insights.claim: Cordova attributes AI companies hitting $100M revenue in months largely to concentrated customer bases (e.g., a few $30–40M defense or big-law deals), contrasting Linear's 40,000 paying customers and historically seat-based model, where hyper-fast growth is much harder.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Investors should discount headline ARR speed for customer concentration.
insights.quote: 40,000 paying customers

insights.claim: Cordova cites Intercom Fin's $1 per AI-resolved support ticket as the ideal outcome-based pricing, but says outcome pricing is hard for features like auto-triaging a bug, so Linear mostly charges usage-based fees tied to its own costs.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Outcome-based pricing works only where value is discrete; expect cost-plus usage pricing in most dev tools.

insights.claim: In Linear's coding sessions, users choose OpenAI or Anthropic models and Linear charges the published API rate plus a small markup; Linear uses frontier models even for its free agent chat and expects to reduce those costs; Loops uses an AI-credit model.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: SaaS layers are passing model costs through with thin markup, making frontier labs the margin capturers on usage.
insights.quote: Here is the published rate and we are adding a little above

insights.claim: Linear keeps seat pricing for the core product and only charges usage for new AI features, typically launched free in beta with advance notice before charging; it prices conservatively high at launch then lowers, rather than starting cheap.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Hybrid seat + usage pricing avoids repricing backlash and protects margins on expensive agent features.

themes.theme: Lean org design and AI-augmented operations

insights.claim: Linear operates on a 'do more with less' principle; Cordova says most companies at Linear's stage and revenue have nearly twice as many employees, and Linear is about 170 people with a flat structure and no executives besides the founders and the COO.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: High revenue per employee and agility; a lean benchmark for dev-tool peers.
insights.quote: we about 170 people

insights.claim: Linear does not outsource support and has built a global in-house support team; Cordova says in 3.5 years she has never had an escalation over dissatisfaction with support, and customers sometimes assume responses are AI because they are so fast.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Support quality as brand moat; deliberate cost choice.

insights.claim: Cordova rejects the model of LLMs auto-answering 100% of support tickets with humans intervening only after angry replies; Linear uses AI to draft responses that humans review, which lets the CX team avoid scaling headcount linearly with the business.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: AI as copilot for headcount leverage rather than replacement; protects brand.

insights.claim: At Linear, sales reps edit website copy and marketers work on revenue data systems, with engineers only reviewing and approving changes — AI tooling lets non-engineers ship changes.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Evidence of AI broadening who can contribute code in software companies.

insights.claim: Cordova uses a Stripe-derived guideline that an engineering-led product company should keep at least ~40% of headcount in engineering, product, design and data; she built a headcount table by function at Linear to track it.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Function mix is a diagnostic for whether a software company stays product-led.

insights.claim: Cordova contrasts Linear with Uber, whose large operations headcount reflects moving people and things, arguing a software business shouldn't need a huge operational component.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Business model should dictate org structure ratios.

insights.claim: Cordova says Stripe, at a $140–160B valuation, tended to always hire someone 'two levels higher' rather than promote existing leaders, which she now sees as a mistake; at Linear she favors growing early team members into scaled leaders.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Retention and internal promotion as cultural differentiator vs hypergrowth upgrading.

themes.theme: Marketing, moats and strategy under rapid change

insights.claim: Before Cordova's arrival, Linear's only marketing was changelog emails, which fewer than 10% of users subscribed to, plus founder tweets; she shifted to in-product announcements since many users open the app daily.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Distribution through the product itself is underused leverage for PLG companies.
insights.quote: less than 10% of users subscribed to the newsletter

insights.claim: Cordova's go-to-market plan aimed to make Linear 'inevitable' — companies are either already on Linear or planning a transition — through brand, storytelling and awareness beyond narrow circles.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Brand inevitability as a strategic goal for category displacement.

insights.claim: Linear now keeps a product roadmap of at most six months and expects its marketing narrative to stay relevant for about six months; Cordova says the new world rewards speed over perfect planning.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Shorter planning horizons across AI-era SaaS; strategy agility is a key competency.

insights.claim: Cordova says many business moats have already collapsed; Linear's edge is a team that keeps its finger on the pulse, since the best model changes daily and unknown companies raise $10B within months.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Durable advantage shifts from structural moats to team speed and adaptability.
insights.quote: there are a lot of business barriers on the market, so to speak, already collapsed

insights.claim: Cordova says Linear joined in a hard 2023 startup market after the 2021–22 funding boom, when companies cut spend and consolidated budgets, which made growth harder given Linear's startup-heavy customer base.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Startup-concentrated SaaS revenue is cyclical with venture funding.

insights.claim: Cordova, a former early-stage investor, says VC is selling money, a commodity, so investors differentiate on operating help, pattern recognition and networks; she felt more useful post product-market fit than pre-PMF.
insights.speaker: Cristina Cordova (COO, Linear)
insights.so_what: Operator-investors have an edge with post-PMF companies.
